𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗳𝗳𝗶𝗰 𝗔𝗱𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗿𝘆 – 𝗥𝗼𝗮𝗱 𝗡𝗼. 𝟮, 𝗕𝗮𝗻𝗷𝗮𝗿𝗮 𝗛𝗶𝗹𝗹𝘀 (𝗙𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝟮𝟳.𝟬𝟮.𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲)

In view of the ongoing construction of Steel Flyover and Underpass works at Jubilee Hills Check Post, KBR Park Entrance and Mugdha Junction under the H-CITI project, pillar works will commence from 27.02.2026 on Road No. 2, Banjara Hills. Traffic congestion is expected between Mugdha Junction, KBR Park Entrance (Gate-I) and Jubilee Hills Check Post. Traffic diversions will be implemented on a need basis.

𝗔𝗹𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗲𝘀 & 𝗗𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀:

• Vehicles from NFCL towards Srinagar Colony, Sagar Society (Mugdha), KBR Park, Jubilee Hills Check Post, Road No. 36/45 and Cable Bridge (Durgam Cheruvu) will be diverted at Srinagar Colony T Junction and Sagar Society via Srinagar Colony Main Road, Indiranagar Labour Adda, Road No. 5 Jubilee Hills, Venkatagiri X Roads (Road No. 10), and then towards Jubilee Hills Check Post.

• Traffic from Road No. 36 & 45 Jubilee Hills heading towards NFCL will be diverted at Jubilee Hills Check Post via Venkatagiri, Road No. 2, Yousufguda Basti, Yousufguda Check Post, Maitrivanam, Ameerpet, Indiranagar Labour Adda, Srinagar Colony and Panjagutta Main Road.

• Commuters from KCP & Road No. 1, Banjara Hills going towards KBR Park, Jubilee Hills Check Post and Road No. 36 may take Road No. 10 via Cancer Hospital, Agrasen Island and Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan to reach Road No. 45 Jubilee Hills.

• Traffic from Masab Tank towards KBR Park and Jubilee Hills Check Post may take a left at Virinchi Hospital (1/12 Junction), proceed via Agrasen Island and Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan to Road No. 45 Jubilee Hills.

𝗔𝗱𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝘁𝗼 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗺𝘂𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀:

• Avoid peak hours (8:30 AM – 11:00 AM & 5:00 PM – 9:00 PM) if possible.
• Follow instructions of traffic police and road signage.
• Use navigation apps for real-time updates.
• Prefer public transport and carpooling.
• Heavy vehicles should avoid the stretch during peak hours.

Commuters are requested to follow updates on the official social media handles of Hyderabad Traffic Police and contact the traffic helpline at 9010203626 for assistance. Citizens are urged to plan their travel accordingly and cooperate with traffic police to ensure smooth traffic flow.

At least 100 houses were razed by fire in Purok Katilingban, Barangay 39, Bacolod City before noon on Friday, Feb. 27, according to Fire Insp. Jemarie Tapiru, deputy city fire marshal.

The blaze was raised to fourth alarm leading to reinforcement from nearby stations, because there weren’t enough firetrucks available, as they were deployed for ashfall clearing operations in Negros Occidental following the recent eruption of Kanlaon Volcano. Fire out was declared at 12:37 p.m. | via Glazyl Masculino

📷 Chamber Volunteer Fire Brigade
